source.stem:
A student wishes to find the volume of a small, irregularly-shaped stone.
A ruler and a measuring cylinder containing some water are available.
Which apparatus is needed?

options.text: neither the ruler nor the measuring cylinder
the ruler and the measuring cylinder

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: North is the direction the north-seeking tip points right now, even while swinging.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: A freely suspended ordinary iron bar always settles north-south.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The red-painted end is the North pole.

mx.name: operation_confusion
mx.teacher_note: Keep the box fixed and turn the needle to its N mark.

intelligence.enrichment: A freely suspended magnet comes to rest along the north-south direction. The end pointing towards north is the North-seeking pole or North pole, and the other end is the South pole; an ordinary iron bar does not always rest along north-south. free suspension of a magnet allows its resting direction to reveal north-south and pole names The learner waits for the suspended magnet or compass needle to come to rest, uses its north-south alignment, and names the north-pointing end as the North pole. A compass or hanging magnet can be read at any moment, and the end labels are just arbitrary names.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Science question. Chapter: Exploring magnets. The student must decide: Use a freely suspended magnet or a compass to find north-south direction and identify the magnet's poles. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names.
